opportunities.gap: The artifact/metadata layer is mislabeled. The MDX teaches feedback templates, but meta.description, learning_objectives[0], the Artifact Studio component (artifact="storyboard frame sequence with narration, signaling, and reader-action notes"), the studio download link, the Adaptive Support 'confusion' bullet, and the Final Check all name the storyboard-frame-sequence artifact. This is the known 192-supplement artifact-mislabel pattern (TOP_TIER P0): the signature artifact for a feedback-templates section should be the feedback template itself, which the MDX body already treats as the artifact ('The artifact is the comment template itself, not a single student's draft', line 52). The mismatch makes the studio instructions incoherent with the lesson.
opportunities.proposed_change: Replace the storyboard-frame-sequence artifact label throughout the metadata/components with a feedback-template artifact (e.g., 'design-draft feedback template with criterion-location-action lines and one prioritized process-level move'). Update meta.description, learning_objectives[0], the <artifact-studio artifact=...> tag, the download-packet link text, the Adaptive Support 'confusion' bullet ('compare a weak and strong version of the feedback template'), and the Final Check sentence so the studio captures a before/after feedback-template revision (the same before/after the Worked Example and Stronger Artifact Standard already describe).

opportunities.gap: The MDX defines WCAG only as 'Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG)' with no version pinned, while the rest of the AIL 606 chapter standard (and the project currency-watch) is WCAG 2.2 AA. An accessibility-specific section that never names the version it audits against is a regression and leaves the AA conformance level (which sets the 4.5:1 and 3:1 contrast floors it relies on) implicit. The course currency-watch explicitly asks to confirm WCAG 2.2 AA is still current vs WCAG 3.0 draft status as of 2026.
opportunities.proposed_change: In the Core Concept paragraph defining WCAG/POUR, pin the version and conformance level explicitly: 'the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 at conformance level AA'. Add a one-line note that WCAG 3.0 remains a W3C Working Draft (not a recommendation) as of 2026, so 2.2 AA is the operative standard. Note that the 4.5:1 / 3:1 contrast floors and the success-criterion IDs (1.1.1, 1.4.1, 1.4.3, 2.1.1, 2.2.1) used in the section are WCAG 2.2 SC IDs.
opportunities.where_to_apply: 05.mdx, Core Concept section, the paragraph beginning 'An accessibility review workflow is a repeatable procedure...' and the POUR sentence; also update the References list.
